beliefs: f removes all whitespace characters (space, tab, newline, and Unicode whitespace) from the string [E1, E2, E3, E7, E9]
f lowercases all letters using Unicode-aware lowercasing [E1, E2, E3, E10]
f capitalizes the first character of the result only if the original string's first character is not whitespace [E2, E3, E8]
leading whitespace (space, tab, etc.) prevents capitalization of the first remaining character [E2, E3, E8]
empty string and all-whitespace strings map to empty string [E1, E2, E3]
digits and punctuation are left unchanged [E1, E2, E3]
capitalization uses str.capitalize semantics: only the first char is uppercased, and if it is ß it becomes 'Ss' (not 'SS'), while ß elsewhere stays lowercase [E11]
the capitalize-first rule uses titlecase-uppercasing of the first char (e.g. ǆ becomes ǅ), not full uppercase [E11]
capitalization is applied to the first surviving character via titlecase-uppercase only (not full str.capitalize), since ẞ (U+1E9E) stays as-is rather than becoming 'Ss' [E12]
the rest of the string is lowercased before capitalization, so mixed-case non-ASCII like Ǆ becomes ǆ then ǅ [E12]
notes: E12 shows ẞ (U+1E9E) is NOT converted to 'Ss' by the capitalize step, so the first-char transform is titlecase-uppercase (which leaves ẞ unchanged) rather than str.capitalize; ß→Ss and ǆ→ǅ still hold. Lowercasing happens first, then titlecase-uppercase of the first char.
